glaciers.name: Sermeq Kujalleq (Jakobshavn Isbræ)
glaciers.note: The fastest-flowing glacier on Earth; drains ~7% of the Greenland Ice Sheet.

glaciers.name: Columbia Glacier
glaciers.note: Textbook tidewater retreat: ~20 km of retreat since the early 1980s.

glaciers.name: Gulkana Glacier
glaciers.note: USGS benchmark glacier; mass balance measured since 1966.

glaciers.name: South Cascade Glacier
glaciers.note: USGS benchmark glacier; mass balance measured since 1959.

glaciers.name: Peyto Glacier
glaciers.note: WGMS reference glacier; feeds the Mistaya → North Saskatchewan rivers.

glaciers.name: Great Aletsch Glacier
glaciers.note: The largest glacier in the Alps.

glaciers.name: Storglaciären
glaciers.note: Longest continuous glacier mass-balance record on Earth (since 1946).

glaciers.name: Khumbu Glacier
glaciers.note: Flows from the Western Cwm through the Khumbu Icefall; lower tongue debris-covered.

glaciers.name: Perito Moreno Glacier
glaciers.note: One of the few Patagonian outlets near balance; periodically dams Lago Argentino.

glaciers.name: Zongo Glacier
glaciers.note: Tropical glacier on Huayna Potosí; meltwater for La Paz hydropower.

glaciers.name: Hintereisferner
glaciers.note: One of the longest glaciological records in the Alps (since 1953).

glaciers.name: Rhône Glacier
glaciers.note: Source of the Rhône; part of its tongue is wrapped in insulating blankets each summer.

glaciers.name: Mer de Glace
glaciers.note: France's longest glacier, on the north side of Mont Blanc.

glaciers.name: Nigardsbreen
glaciers.note: Outlet of Jostedalsbreen, mainland Europe's largest ice cap.

glaciers.name: Wolverine Glacier
glaciers.note: USGS benchmark glacier in a wet maritime climate.

glaciers.name: Lemon Creek Glacier
glaciers.note: Juneau Icefield glacier with a mass-balance record since 1953.

glaciers.name: Chhota Shigri Glacier
glaciers.note: Benchmark glacier of the western Himalaya.

glaciers.name: Brewster Glacier
glaciers.note: One of the few glaciers in New Zealand with a field mass-balance record.

glaciers.name: Pasterze
glaciers.note: Austria's largest glacier, below the Grossglockner.

glaciers.name: Helheim Glacier
glaciers.note: One of East Greenland's largest outlets; it sped up sharply in the mid-2000s.

glaciers.name: Thwaites Glacier
glaciers.note: Drains into the Amundsen Sea; the ice it holds could raise sea level by ~65 cm.

glaciers.name: Pine Island Glacier
glaciers.note: With Thwaites, the fastest-changing glacier in West Antarctica.

glaciers.name: Hubbard Glacier
glaciers.note: North America's largest tidewater glacier — and, unusually, advancing.

glaciers.name: Baltoro Glacier
glaciers.note: About 63 km long below K2: one of the longest glaciers outside the polar regions.

glaciers.name: Breiðamerkurjökull
glaciers.note: Vatnajökull outlet calving into the Jökulsárlón lagoon.

glaciers.name: Silvretta Glacier
glaciers.note: Mass balance measured since 1919 — one of the two longest series anywhere.

glaciers.name: Claridenfirn
glaciers.note: The longest glaciological series on Earth: stakes read every year since 1914.

glaciers.name: Gries Glacier
glaciers.note: Measured since 1962; it ends in a hydropower reservoir on the Italian border.

glaciers.name: Taku Glacier
glaciers.note: Advanced for a century while its neighbours retreated; turned to retreat around 2018.

glaciers.name: Storbreen
glaciers.note: Continental-climate Norwegian glacier, measured since 1949.

glaciers.name: Engabreen
glaciers.note: Svartisen outlet with a hydropower laboratory tunnelled beneath its bed.

glaciers.name: Midtre Lovénbreen
glaciers.note: High-Arctic valley glacier beside Ny-Ålesund, measured since 1968.

glaciers.name: Kongsvegen
glaciers.note: A surge-type glacier, quiescent and slow since its 1948 surge.

glaciers.name: White Glacier
glaciers.note: The longest mass-balance record in the Canadian High Arctic (since 1960).

glaciers.name: Urumqi Glacier No. 1
glaciers.note: China's reference glacier; it split into two branches in 1993.

glaciers.name: Tuyuksu Glacier
glaciers.note: Above Almaty; the longest record in Central Asia (since 1957).

glaciers.name: Abramov Glacier
glaciers.note: Its research station was abandoned in 1999; measurements resumed in 2011.

glaciers.name: Echaurren Norte
glaciers.note: The Southern Hemisphere's longest series; feeds Santiago's water supply.

glaciers.name: Djankuat Glacier
glaciers.note: Caucasus reference glacier, measured since 1968.

glaciers.name: Yala Glacier
glaciers.note: Small clean-ice Himalayan glacier; one of the few measured in Nepal.

glaciers.name: Bahía del Diablo Glacier
glaciers.note: The only long field mass-balance record on the Antarctic Peninsula.

glaciers.name: Athabasca Glacier
glaciers.note: The most visited glacier in North America, beside the Icefields Parkway.

glaciers.name: Franz Josef Glacier / Kā Roimata o Hine Hukatere
glaciers.note: Steep, fast and maritime: it once descended into temperate rainforest.

glaciers.name: Petermann Glacier
glaciers.note: Ends in a floating ice tongue that calved 260 km² islands in 2010 and 2012.

glaciers.name: Kangerlussuaq Glacier
glaciers.note: One of East Greenland's three largest outlets; it sped up sharply around 2005.

glaciers.name: Lambert Glacier
glaciers.note: Often called the largest glacier on Earth: it drains ~8% of the Antarctic Ice Sheet.

glaciers.name: Malaspina Glacier
glaciers.note: The largest piedmont glacier on Earth, a lobe of ice spread onto the coastal plain.

glaciers.name: Fedchenko Glacier
glaciers.note: About 77 km long, the longest glacier outside the polar regions; the line drawn covers its middle trunk (the tongue lies in the next satellite tile).
